title: Minimax Prediction of Monotone Score-Averaged Treatment Effects with Rough Full-Dimensional Nuisances

tldr:
On the exact known-uniform-design benchmark with full-dimensional Hölder-\(s\) treatment and outcome regressions and only a monotone 1-Lipschitz score-averaged causal target, the integrated predictive minimax risk has order
\[
 n^{-2/3}+n^{-b_*},\qquad
 b_*=\begin{cases}8s/(6s+d),&0<s\le1/2,\\8s/(4s+d+1),&1/2\le s\le1.\end{cases}
\]
A total original-record predictor with quadratic and cubic retained-weight corrections attains it, and normalized original-law mixtures prove the converse. There is no logarithmic factor. Exact same-class oracle survival is \(8s\ge d+\min\{2s,1\}\), including equality. For every \(0<s\le1\), explicit histogram nuisance fits evaluate the anchor's first-order squared sufficient predictive guarantee as \(O_P(n^{-2/3}+n^{-4s/(2s+d)})\), whose oracle polynomial range is \(4s\ge d\). The higher-order nuisance exponent is strictly larger everywhere and the total guaranteed power improves when \(4s<d\). This compares an in-probability first-order guarantee with a uniform expected-risk theorem on the restricted benchmark.
gap: Published reduced-effect and calibration guarantees control first-stage remainders but do not evaluate the matching predictive minimax frontier under smoothness of the score average alone. Published full-contrast reduction and directional higher-order theorems impose restrictions absent from \(\mathcal M(s,d)\).
fill: An evaluated two-sided rate, total observable attainment, original-law testing lower, and exact same-class oracle-survival set would quantify this limitation across every fixed public \((s,d)\). The candidate boundary \(8s\ge d+\min\{2s,1\}\) is an explicit hypothesis for this same-class comparison; proving it includes deciding the equality logarithms.
